## What's new in 1.5.1

- **Smooth network switching.** Moving between Wi-Fi, mobile data, another Wi-Fi or a VPN (WireGuard, OpenVPN, Tailscale) no longer needs a restart of the app or its background service.
  - The app notices the network change within about 2 seconds. It drops connections that can't work any more, checks the rest, restarts LAN discovery on the new network and reconnects to your peers right away.
  - Connections that silently died (which used to make a peer look connected while nothing got through) are detected and replaced: quiet links are checked every 5 seconds and closed after 15 seconds without an answer.
- **Calls survive a network switch.** If the connection breaks during a call, the app dials the other side again and the call continues by itself, showing **Reconnecting…** meanwhile. A call now ends only after 15 seconds without any contact (was 8). If the other device's app was closed, the call still ends at once.
- **Peers reachable several ways.** The app remembers every address a peer was seen at (home Wi-Fi, Tailscale, WireGuard, …) and tries them all, so it still finds the peer over the VPN after you leave the Wi-Fi.
- **Fix: "sometimes cannot connect".** Seeing a peer on the local network used to overwrite its saved VPN address, so it became unreachable once you left that Wi-Fi. A saved address is now only updated when the peer gets a new address on the same network.
- Peers added by name (e.g. a Tailscale MagicDNS name) resolve to IPv4 and every address found is tried.

Upgrading: install over 1.2.0 or newer (same variant on Android). Settings and saved peers are kept. 1.5.1 works with 1.2.0 – 1.4.0, but update **both** devices: an older device on the other end keeps using its old, dead connection and may still drop the call after 8 seconds. Versions before 1.2.0 (including 1.1.1) can't connect, because they don't encrypt.
